_readme: Heuristic weights (0-100 scale) for Android permissions that are commonly abused by malware families (banking trojans, spyware, ransomware). Contributions are summed and capped when scoring an installed app; this is one signal among several, not a standalone verdict.

permissions.reason: Device admin can block uninstallation — common ransomware/lockware pattern
Accessibility services can read screen content and inject input — used by banking trojans for overlay/keylogging attacks
Can modify secure system settings, normally restricted to system apps
Can read all notifications, including one-time-password codes
Can draw overlays on top of other apps — used for phishing overlays and clickjacking
Can prompt installation of additional APKs — dropper behavior
Can intercept incoming SMS, including OTP/2FA codes
Can read stored SMS messages, including OTP/2FA codes
Can observe which apps the user is using, often paired with overlay attacks
Can monitor or redirect outgoing calls
Can send SMS silently, e.g. premium-rate SMS fraud
Broad access to all files on shared storage
Can record audio in the background
Can exfiltrate the user's contact list
Can place calls without user confirmation
Can read device identifiers and call state
Can enumerate every other app installed on the device
